categories.label: Buck converters
categories.blurb: Step a battery or 12–48 V supply down to 5 V or 3.3 V for the MCU, servos and sensors.

filters.label: Highest input
filters.help: Fully charged battery or supply maximum, plus spikes. 4S LiPo = 16.8 V, 6S = 25.2 V.

categories.label: Battery chargers
categories.blurb: Charge Li-ion, LiPo, LiFePO4 or NiMH packs from USB, a DC jack or a solar panel.

filters.label: Input voltage
filters.help: 5 for USB, 9–20 for USB-PD, 12 / 24 for a DC jack.

categories.label: Communication ICs
categories.blurb: CAN-FD, RS-485, EtherCAT, Ethernet and USB-serial chips for motor controllers, smart servos and robot buses.

filters.label: MCU logic level
filters.help: 3.3 for most MCUs, 1.8 for some SoCs.

filters.label: Bus fault protection
filters.help: Survives a short to the motor supply. 24 V robots: ≥ ±40 V.

categories.label: Cameras
categories.blurb: DVP and MIPI image sensors, SPI cameras and AI vision cameras that track objects for you.

filters.label: On-chip JPEG
filters.help: Lets small MCUs stream or store frames.

categories.label: LiDAR & ToF
categories.blurb: Time-of-flight sensors, single-point LiDARs and 360° scanners for obstacle avoidance and SLAM.

commonFilters.label: Hand-solderable
commonFilters.help: SOIC, SOT, TSSOP, MSOP or a module — no QFN/BGA/LGA.

components.name: TPS54202
components.description: Cheap 28 V, 2 A synchronous buck in SOT-23-6: the default way to make 5 V or 3.3 V from a 12 V rail or a 3S/4S battery.

components.name: TPS563201
components.description: Very cheap 17 V, 3 A synchronous buck in SOT-23-6 with D-CAP2 fast transient response, for 5 V/3.3 V rails from 12 V.

components.name: TPS54302
components.description: 28 V, 3 A synchronous buck in SOT-23-6 with internal compensation: a drop-in upgrade of the TPS54202 for heavier 5 V loads.

components.name: TPS62933
components.description: 30 V, 3 A synchronous buck in a tiny SOT-583 with 12 µA quiescent current and adjustable 200 kHz–2.2 MHz switching: good for battery robots.

components.name: TPS62160
components.description: 17 V, 1 A synchronous buck in a 2×2 mm WSON with power-good and 17 µA quiescent current, for small 3.3 V logic rails from 5–12 V.

components.name: TPS62130
components.description: 17 V, 3 A synchronous buck in a 3×3 mm QFN with power-good, soft-start/tracking and pin-selectable 2.5/1.25 MHz, for compact 3.3 V/5 V rails.

components.name: TPS54360
components.description: 60 V, 3.5 A non-synchronous buck with Eco-mode, for robots running on 24 V, 36 V or 48 V packs that need a few amps of 5 V or 12 V.

components.name: TPS54560B
components.description: 60 V, 5 A non-synchronous buck with Eco-mode, for powering servos or an SBC from 24–48 V robot batteries.

components.name: LMR33630
components.description: 36 V, 3 A synchronous buck with power-good, 25 µA quiescent current and internal compensation, for 24 V robots and 6S–8S LiPo packs.

components.name: LMR36510
components.description: 65 V, 1 A synchronous buck with power-good and 26 µA quiescent current, a small rugged 5 V/3.3 V logic supply for 48 V systems.

components.name: LMR51430
components.description: 36 V, 3 A synchronous buck in SOT-23-6, pin-compatible with the TPS54202, for 24 V robots that want the cheap SOT-23 layout.

components.name: AP63203
components.description: Fixed 3.3 V, 2 A synchronous buck from up to 32 V in TSOT-23-6 with no feedback resistors and 22 µA quiescent current: the simplest MCU supply.
components.summary: 3.8–32 V in → 3.3 V fixed, 2 A, 1.1 MHz

components.name: AP63205
components.description: Fixed 5 V, 2 A synchronous buck from up to 32 V in TSOT-23-6 with no feedback resistors, for servo/USB 5 V rails on 12–24 V robots.
components.summary: 3.8–32 V in → 5 V fixed, 2 A, 1.1 MHz

components.name: AP62300
components.description: Low-cost 18 V, 3 A synchronous COT buck in TSOT-23-6 or SOT-563 for 3.3 V/5 V rails from 5 V or 12 V inputs.

components.name: MP1584EN
components.description: The 28 V, 3 A non-synchronous buck found on countless mini buck modules; adjustable 100 kHz–1.5 MHz, OK for repairs and clones of those boards.

components.name: MP2315S
components.description: 24 V, 3 A synchronous buck in TSOT-23-8 with a selectable power-save (AAM) mode, the core of many 5 V mini modules and a good 12 V-to-5 V part.

components.name: SY8089A
components.description: Very cheap 5.5 V, 2 A synchronous 1 MHz buck in SOT-23-5 for making 3.3 V or 1.8 V from USB 5 V or a single Li-ion cell.

components.name: LM2596
components.description: Classic 40 V, 3 A, 150 kHz non-synchronous buck in TO-263: robust and forgiving, but big and inefficient next to modern synchronous parts.

components.name: XL4015
components.description: Cheap 36 V, 5 A, 180 kHz non-synchronous buck in TO-263-5, the chip on the popular 5 A adjustable buck/CC-CV modules.

components.name: TPS5430
components.description: Proven 36 V, 3 A non-synchronous 500 kHz buck with internal compensation in a PowerPAD SOIC-8, for 24 V robot rails.

components.name: LM5164
components.description: 100 V, 1 A synchronous COT buck with power-good and 10.5 µA quiescent current, for 48 V and 60 V+ robot or e-bike packs.

components.name: Pololu D24V22F5 5 V step-down regulator
components.description: Tiny 5 V synchronous buck module (up to 36 V in, about 2.2–2.5 A) with enable and power-good, a solid drop-in 5 V supply for small robots.
components.summary: 5.3–36 V in → 5 V fixed, 2.2 A, 400 kHz

components.name: Pololu D36V28F5 5 V step-down regulator
components.description: 5 V, 3.2 A synchronous buck module for up to 50 V in, with enable, power-good and reverse protection: good for 24–36 V robots and 10S packs.
components.summary: 5.3–50 V in → 5 V fixed, 3.2 A, 500 kHz

components.name: Pololu D24V50F5 5 V, 5 A step-down regulator
components.description: 5 V, 5 A synchronous buck module for 6–38 V in with an enable pin, sized for servos, motor drivers or a Raspberry Pi on 3S–8S batteries.
components.summary: 6–38 V in → 5 V fixed, 5 A, 600 kHz

components.name: MP1584 mini adjustable buck module
components.description: Tiny (23×17 mm) adjustable buck board, 4.5–28 V in to 0.8–20 V out, for wiring a cheap 5 V or 3.3 V supply into a hobby robot.

components.name: LM2596S adjustable buck module
components.description: Ubiquitous 43×21 mm LM2596S adjustable buck board, up to 40 V in and 1.25–35 V out, for quick bench and hobby supplies.

components.name: XL4015 adjustable 5 A buck module with voltmeter
components.description: XL4015 adjustable buck board with a built-in voltmeter and screw terminals, 1.25–32 V out at up to 4 A, for higher-current hobby rails.

components.name: OV2640 2MP DVP camera module
components.description: The classic 2 MP camera of the ESP32-CAM. On-chip JPEG lets an ESP32 or STM32 (DCMI) grab and stream frames over Wi-Fi with little processing. Sold as cheap 24-pin FPC modules with many lens angles.

components.name: OV3660 3MP DVP camera module
components.description: A 3 MP BSI sensor with on-chip JPEG that drops into OV2640 sockets on ESP32-CAM-style boards. Gives sharper frames and 60 fps at VGA for MCU vision projects.

components.name: OV5640 5MP DVP/MIPI camera module
components.description: A 5 MP sensor with on-chip JPEG, a VCM autofocus driver and both DVP and 2-lane MIPI outputs. It's the high-end choice for ESP32-S3, STM32 DCMI and RP2040 cameras, and it does 90 fps at VGA.

components.name: OV7670 VGA DVP camera module
components.description: A cheap VGA (0.3 MP) sensor with no JPEG, used in many Arduino/STM32/FPGA tutorials. Good for line following or blob tracking at QVGA, but you must buffer raw frames yourself.

components.name: GC0308 VGA DVP camera module
components.description: A low-cost, low-power (70 mW) VGA sensor on 24-pin FPC modules. It's on the M5Stack CoreS3 and fits barcode/QR reading and simple obstacle or colour detection on ESP32 and K210 robots.

components.name: GC2145 2MP DVP/MIPI camera module
components.description: A 2 MP UXGA sensor, now the usual low-cost replacement for the OV2640 on ESP32 and other MCU boards. Offers DVP plus 1/2-lane MIPI but no JPEG encoder.

components.name: Himax HM0360 low-power VGA mono camera
components.description: An ultra-low-power BSI monochrome VGA sensor for always-on TinyML vision (person detection, wake-on-motion). Draws about 8 mA at VGA 60 fps and a few hundred µA in monitor mode. Runs on an RP2040, Arduino or Cortex-M.

components.name: Arducam 5MP OV5647 Mini Camera for Raspberry Pi
components.description: A cheap 5 MP MIPI CSI-2 camera with the same OV5647 sensor as the original Raspberry Pi Camera v1.3, natively supported by libcamera. A low-cost choice for Pi-based robots and the Grove Vision AI V2.

components.name: Raspberry Pi Camera Module 2
components.description: The official 8 MP Sony IMX219 camera for Raspberry Pi. It's small (25×24 mm, 3 g) and cheap, and does 640×480 at up to 206 fps for fast tracking.

components.name: Raspberry Pi Camera Module 3
components.description: The official 12 MP Sony IMX708 camera with fast phase-detect autofocus and HDR, on the same 25×24 mm board as Camera Module 2. A good general-purpose camera for Pi robots: 1080p50 and 120 fps at 1536×864.

components.name: Raspberry Pi Camera Module 3 Wide
components.description: Camera Module 3 with a 120° diagonal wide lens: 12 MP IMX708, PDAF autofocus and HDR. Good for robot navigation, obstacle avoidance and room-scale views where a 75° lens is too narrow.

components.name: Raspberry Pi High Quality Camera
components.description: A 12.3 MP Sony IMX477 camera with a 7.9 mm-diagonal sensor and interchangeable C/CS- or M12-mount lenses. Pick it when a robot needs good low-light performance, telephoto or specialist optics.

components.name: Raspberry Pi Global Shutter Camera
components.description: A 1.6 MP Sony IMX296 global-shutter camera with large 3.45 µm pixels and C/CS lenses. Gives distortion-free frames of fast motion for machine vision, visual odometry and high-speed robots. Up to 60 fps.

components.name: Arducam OV9281 1MP Global Shutter Mono Camera (Raspberry Pi)
components.description: A 1 MP monochrome global-shutter MIPI camera with a NoIR M12 lens. Gives fast (up to 143 fps), skew-free frames for AprilTag/ArUco tracking, visual odometry and IR-illuminated robot vision on a Pi or Jetson.

components.name: Raspberry Pi AI Camera
components.description: A 12.3 MP Sony IMX500 camera that runs neural networks (object detection, pose) on the sensor itself and returns tensor metadata with each frame. The host Pi stays free for the rest of the robot software.

components.name: Arducam Mini 2MP Plus SPI camera
components.description: An OV2640 camera with an 8 MB frame buffer and JPEG, controlled over SPI + I²C. Lets any MCU, even an Arduino Uno, capture 2 MP stills without a camera interface or PSRAM. Uses an M12 lens.

mcuNeeds.name: SPI camera (with frame buffer)
mcuNeeds.needs: an I²C bus, an SPI bus + chip-select

components.name: DFRobot HuskyLens (K210)
components.description: A no-code AI vision sensor with a K210 processor and 2" screen. It learns faces, objects, colours, lines and tags at the press of a button and sends bounding boxes to an Arduino, micro:bit or ESP32 over UART or I²C.

components.name: DFRobot HuskyLens 2 (K230)
components.description: The second-generation HuskyLens: a 6 TOPS Kendryte K230 with 20+ built-in models (detection, pose, segmentation, plates), custom model deployment and a 2.4" touchscreen. Sends results to an MCU over UART/I²C.

components.name: Pixy2 (CMUcam5) smart camera
components.description: A small 60 fps vision sensor that learns colour objects and tracks lines, intersections and road signs on board, with built-in LED lighting. It returns object blocks to an Arduino or Pi over SPI, I²C, UART or USB.

components.name: OpenMV Cam RT1062
components.description: A MicroPython-programmable machine-vision camera: 600 MHz i.MX RT1062, 32 MB SDRAM, a 5 MP OV5640 on an M12 mount, plus Wi-Fi/BT, CAN, Ethernet (PoE) and servo outputs. Runs vision code and ML models.

components.name: Seeed Grove Vision AI Module V2
components.description: A low-cost TinyML vision board with a Himax WiseEye2 HX6538 (dual Cortex-M55 + Ethos-U55 NPU) and a CSI port for an OV5647 camera. Runs YOLO/MobileNet models and reports results to an MCU over I²C (Grove) or UART.

components.name: Arducam OV9281 1MP Global Shutter USB Camera
components.description: A plug-and-play UVC webcam board with a 1 MP mono global-shutter OV9281 that streams 100 fps MJPEG at 1280×800. Good for fiducial tracking and visual odometry on a Pi, Jetson or PC.
components.summary: OV9281, 1.02 MP 1280×800, USB, global shutter, JPEG

components.name: MCP73831
components.description: Tiny 500 mA linear charger for one Li-ion/LiPo cell from USB, with a single tri-state STAT pin; the classic choice for small boards.

components.name: TP4056
components.description: Ultra-cheap 1 A linear charger for one Li-ion cell in ESOP-8, with CHRG/STDBY LED outputs and an NTC input; the chip on most blue USB charger boards.

components.name: TP4057
components.description: 500 mA linear Li-ion charger in SOT-23-6 with battery reverse-polarity protection and two open-drain status pins (CHRG, STDBY).

components.name: BQ21040
components.description: 0.8 A linear charger for one 4.2 V Li-ion cell in SOT-23-6, 30 V input rating with 6.6 V OVP, NTC input and a CHG status pin.

components.name: BQ24074
components.description: 1.5 A linear Li-ion charger with power path: OUT runs the system from USB/DC while the battery charges, with selectable 100/500 mA USB limits and VIN-DPM.

components.name: MCP73871
components.description: 1 A linear Li-ion charger with load sharing (power path), USB 100/500 mA selection, VPCC input-voltage regulation for solar, and STAT1/STAT2/PG outputs.

components.name: BQ25170
components.description: 800 mA linear charger for one Li-ion or LiFePO4 cell in a 2x2 mm WSON; a VSET resistor picks 3.5–3.7 V (LiFePO4) or 4.05–4.4 V (Li-ion).

components.name: BQ25172
components.description: 800 mA linear charger for 1–6 series NiMH cells in a 2x2 mm WSON: cell count by VSET resistor, timer-based termination, NTC input and a STAT pin.

components.name: CN3058E
components.description: Low-cost 1 A linear charger for one LiFePO4 cell (3.6 V, adjustable up with a resistor) with CHRG/DONE outputs and an NTC input, in ESOP-8.

components.name: BQ25895
components.description: I²C 5 A buck charger for one Li-ion cell with NVDC power path, BC1.2 D+/D- detection, 3.1 A 5 V boost (OTG), ADC and up to 14 V input.

components.name: BQ25601
components.description: I²C 3 A buck charger for one Li-ion cell with NVDC power path, 1.2 A USB OTG boost, PSEL USB/adapter input select and STAT/PG outputs.

components.name: BQ25798
components.description: I²C 5 A buck-boost charger for 1–4 series Li-ion/LiFePO4 cells from 3.6–24 V (USB-PD), with solar MPPT, dual-input mux, OTG up to 22 V and NVDC power path.

components.name: BQ25887
components.description: I²C 2 A boost charger that charges a 2S Li-ion pack from 5 V USB, with integrated cell balancing, 16-bit ADC, NTC input and STAT/PG outputs.

components.name: BQ24650
components.description: Standalone synchronous buck charge controller for solar: input-voltage-regulation MPPT, 5–28 V panel, 1–6 cell Li-ion, LiFePO4 or lead-acid, up to 10 A.

components.name: CN3791
components.description: Cheap 4 A PWM buck charge controller for one 4.2 V Li-ion cell from a 4.5–28 V solar panel, with constant-voltage MPPT and CHRG/DONE outputs.

components.name: BQ25504
components.description: Nano-power boost charger for energy harvesting: cold-starts at 600 mV, harvests down to 130 mV from small solar cells or TEGs with MPPT, into a Li-ion cell or supercap.

components.name: IP2312
components.description: 5 V input, 3 A synchronous buck charger for one Li-ion cell in ESOP-8 with NTC protection, two LED status drivers and adaptive input current.

components.name: IP2326
components.description: 15 W boost charger for 2S or 3S Li-ion packs from a 5 V (or QC fast-charge) USB input, with 2S cell balancing, NTC input and status/LED outputs, in QFN-24.

components.name: IP5306
components.description: Power-bank SoC in ESOP-8: 2.1 A switching Li-ion charger plus 5 V 2.1 A boost output with one inductor, 4-LED fuel gauge and a power key.

components.name: BQ25713
components.description: I²C NVDC buck-boost charge controller for 1–4S packs from 3.5–24 V (USB-C PD), up to 8.1 A charge, OTG output 3–20.8 V and system power monitor.

components.name: Adafruit Universal USB/DC/Solar LiPo Charger (BQ24074)
components.description: BQ24074 breakout with USB-C, DC jack and JST ports: charges one LiPo at up to 1.5 A from 5–10 V USB, DC or a 6 V solar panel, with a load-sharing output.

components.name: Adafruit PowerBoost 1000C
components.description: MCP73871 load-sharing LiPo charger (1 A from micro-USB) plus a TPS61090 5.2 V boost for 1 A+ output, with enable and low-battery pins: a small UPS for 5 V projects.

components.name: Adafruit Micro-Lipo Charger (USB-C)
components.description: Tiny MCP73831 LiPo charger with a USB-C jack and JST-PH battery plug: 100 mA by default, 500 mA with a solder jumper, red/green charge LEDs.

components.name: DFRobot Solar Power Manager 5V
components.description: Solar/USB charger board for one Li-ion cell (CN3165, 900 mA, constant-voltage MPPT for 5–6 V panels) with a 5 V 1 A boosted output and battery protection.

components.name: SparkFun LiPo Charger Plus
components.description: USB-C single-cell LiPo charger board using the MCP73833: up to 1 A, selectable charge rate, optional NTC thermistor, charge/power/done LEDs and two JST ports.

components.name: TCAN1042HV
components.description: TI ±70 V fault-protected CAN FD transceiver with a VIO pin for 3.3 V MCUs and standby with remote wake. A robust pick for CAN/CAN FD links to motor controllers on 24-48 V robot power buses.

components.name: TJA1051T/3
components.description: Very common, cheap CAN FD transceiver (5 Mbit/s) with a VIO pin for 3.3 V MCUs. The default PHY for motor-controller CAN buses (ODrive-style drives, robot joints) when no sleep/wake is needed.

components.name: TJA1042T/3
components.description: CAN FD transceiver (5 Mbit/s) with VIO for 3.3 V MCUs and a very-low-current standby with bus wake-up. Good for battery-powered robots whose CAN nodes need to sleep.

components.name: TJA1443
components.description: CAN FD transceiver (5 Mbit/s) with sleep mode: battery-powered wake receiver, INH output to switch the node's regulator, WAKE pin and ERR_N diagnostics. For robots that power down whole nodes and wake them over CAN.

components.name: MCP2562FD
components.description: CAN FD transceiver with a 1.8-5.5 V VIO pin and 5 µA standby with bus wake. Works straight from 1.8/3.3 V MCUs; a common pick for CAN FD links to motor drivers and sensor nodes.

components.name: MCP2542FD
components.description: CAN FD transceiver specified up to 8 Mbit/s, with a 1.7-5.5 V VIO for low-voltage MCUs and 4 µA standby with wake on CAN activity. Suits fast CAN FD buses to motor drivers and sensor hubs.

components.name: CA-IF1042LVS
components.description: Low-cost Chipanalog CAN FD transceiver (5 Mbit/s), pin-compatible with the TCAN1042V, with VIO for 3.3 V MCUs and standby with remote wake. A budget second source for CAN FD motor-controller buses.

components.name: SIT1042AT/3
components.description: Low-cost TJA1042T/3-compatible CAN FD transceiver (5 Mbit/s) with VIO for 3.3 V MCUs, ±70 V bus protection and standby with bus wake-up. A cheap, well-stocked option for CAN FD robot buses.

components.name: SN65HVD230
components.description: Cheap 3.3 V classic CAN transceiver (1 Mbit/s) in SOIC-8, a direct match for 3.3 V MCUs with a CAN peripheral (STM32 bxCAN, ESP32 TWAI). Fine for CAN 2.0 links to hobby motor controllers. Not CAN FD.

components.name: MCP2551
components.description: Classic 5 V CAN 2.0 transceiver (1 Mbit/s, ±42 V bus pins) found in many older robot and hobby CAN designs. Not recommended for new designs: use the MCP2561/MCP2562FD instead.

components.name: ISO1042
components.description: 5 kVrms isolated CAN FD transceiver (5 Mbit/s, ±70 V bus fault, ±30 V common mode). Breaks ground loops on CAN FD links to motor drives and battery packs. Needs an isolated 5 V supply on the bus side.
components.summary: CAN-FD transceiver, 5 Mbit/s, CAN TX/RX, isolated

components.name: ISO1044
components.description: Low-cost 3 kVrms isolated CAN FD transceiver (5 Mbit/s, ±58 V bus fault) in a plain narrow SOIC-8. A compact way to isolate a CAN FD link to motor controllers. Needs an isolated 5 V supply on the bus side.
components.summary: CAN-FD transceiver, 5 Mbit/s, CAN TX/RX, isolated

components.name: ISOW1044
components.description: 5 kVrms isolated CAN FD transceiver (5 Mbit/s, ±58 V) with a built-in isolated DC-DC, a spare isolated GPIO and standby with bus wake-up. A one-chip isolated CAN FD node for motor drives on a 5 V rail.
components.summary: CAN-FD transceiver, 5 Mbit/s, CAN TX/RX, isolated

components.name: ADM3053
components.description: Isolated classic CAN transceiver with a built-in isoPower DC-DC (2.5 kVrms, 1 Mbit/s): one 5 V rail powers both sides, no separate isolated supply. Good for CANopen nodes on robot arms. Not CAN FD.
components.summary: CAN 2.0 transceiver, 1 Mbit/s, CAN TX/RX, isolated

components.name: MCP2515
components.description: Classic CAN 2.0B controller on SPI (1 Mbit/s, 3 TX / 2 RX buffers, 6 filters). Needs an external CAN transceiver. Adds a CAN port to MCUs or SBCs without one, for legacy CAN motor drivers and sensors.

components.name: MCP2518FD
components.description: CAN FD controller on SPI (1 Mbit/s arbitration, 8 Mbit/s data, 31 FIFOs, 32 filters). Pair it with a CAN FD transceiver to add a CAN FD motor or sensor bus to any MCU or SBC.

components.name: MCP251863
components.description: MCP2518FD CAN FD controller plus ATA6563 transceiver in one package, SPI to the host, 5 Mbit/s data phase. A one-chip CAN FD port to motor controllers from a 3.3 V MCU (the transceiver needs 5 V).

components.name: TCAN4550
components.description: Bosch M_CAN CAN FD controller and transceiver in one package, on SPI (18 MHz), with a 5 V LDO, WAKE pin and INH. Runs straight off a 12/24 V battery to give any MCU a CAN FD motor or sensor bus.

components.name: TCAN4550-Q1
components.description: Automotive TCAN4550: M_CAN CAN FD controller, transceiver and 5 V/70 mA LDO on SPI, 8 Mbit/s, ±58 V bus. Pin-compatible upgrade of the TCAN4550 for 12/24 V robot CAN FD buses.

components.name: MAX3485
components.description: 3.3 V half-duplex RS-485/RS-422 transceiver, 10 Mbit/s, 32 nodes, standard 75176 pinout in SOIC-8. The classic way to put a 3.3 V MCU UART on a Modbus RTU or smart-servo bus.

components.name: SP3485
components.description: Very cheap 3.3 V half-duplex RS-485/RS-422 transceiver, 10 Mbit/s, 32 nodes, 75176 pinout. A JLCPCB basic-style part for Modbus sensors, RS-485 servo buses and robot sub-networks.

components.name: THVD1450
components.description: Robust 3-5.5 V half-duplex RS-485 transceiver: 50 Mbit/s, ±30 kV HBM / ±18 kV IEC ESD, ±18 V bus pins, 256 nodes. Good for fast smart-servo buses and noisy motor-drive cabling.

components.name: MAX485
components.description: Classic 5 V half-duplex RS-485/RS-422 transceiver, 2.5 Mbit/s, 32 nodes, 75176 pinout. The chip on most cheap RS-485 modules, for Modbus or servo links on 5 V systems.

components.name: MAX13487E
components.description: 5 V half-duplex RS-485 transceiver with AutoDirection: no DE pin, the chip switches direction itself. 500 kbit/s, 128 nodes, ±15 kV ESD. Handy for UART-only links to Modbus devices or smart servos.

components.name: ADM2587E
components.description: Isolated RS-485/RS-422 transceiver with a built-in isoPower DC-DC: 2.5 kVrms, 500 kbit/s, ±15 kV ESD, 256 nodes, single 3.3 or 5 V supply. Breaks ground loops on long Modbus or motor-drive runs.
components.summary: RS-485 / Modbus transceiver, 500 kbit/s, UART, isolated

components.name: ISO1410
components.description: 5 kVrms isolated half-duplex RS-485 transceiver, 500 kbit/s, ±30 kV HBM, 256 nodes, 1.8-5 V logic side. Needs a separate isolated bus supply. For ground-loop-free Modbus links to drives and battery packs.
components.summary: RS-485 / Modbus transceiver, 500 kbit/s, UART, isolated

components.name: MAX3232E
components.description: 3-5.5 V dual RS-232 driver/receiver with a built-in charge pump (4 small caps), 250 kbit/s, ±15 kV ESD on line pins. Connects an MCU UART to RS-232 gear: GPS, lidars, legacy motor controllers, PCs.

components.name: TJA1021
components.description: LIN 2.x / ISO 17987 transceiver (up to 20 kBd) with sleep mode, bus and local wake-up, and an INH output to switch the node's regulator. Drives cheap automotive LIN actuators and sensors from an MCU UART on a 12 V robot.

components.name: LAN8720A
components.description: Low-cost 10/100 Ethernet PHY with RMII in a 4x4 mm QFN. Pairs with an MCU's built-in Ethernet MAC (STM32, ESP32) for a robot's wired link to a PC, ROS 2 host or Ethernet sensors.

components.name: KSZ8081RNA
components.description: Single-3.3 V 10/100 Ethernet PHY with RMII in a 4x4 mm QFN; makes the 50 MHz RMII clock from a 25 MHz crystal and has LinkMD cable diagnostics. A solid PHY for an MCU-based robot's Ethernet port.

components.name: DP83848
components.description: Robust 10/100 Ethernet PHY with MII or RMII in an easy-to-solder LQFP-48, used in many STM32/NXP MAC reference designs. A classic choice for a robot controller's wired Ethernet port.

components.name: W5500
components.description: SPI Ethernet chip with hardwired TCP/IP, MAC and integrated 10/100 PHY: gives any MCU, even one without a MAC, wired Ethernet with 8 hardware sockets. Good for UDP/TCP telemetry and control links on small robots.

components.name: ENC28J60
components.description: Stand-alone 10BASE-T Ethernet MAC+PHY on SPI with an 8 KB packet buffer. Adds basic wired Ethernet to MCUs without a MAC; fine for slow telemetry or config links, but needs a software TCP/IP stack (lwIP).

components.name: LAN9252
components.description: 2/3-port EtherCAT slave controller (Beckhoff ESC) with two integrated 100BASE-TX PHYs; the host MCU talks to it over SPI/SQI or a parallel bus. The standard way to build EtherCAT servo drives, joint modules or I/O nodes for a robot arm.

components.name: AX58100
components.description: 2/3-port EtherCAT slave controller with two 100BASE-TX PHYs plus on-chip PWM, step/dir, encoder input and SPI master. Can run a simple EtherCAT motor or joint node with little MCU code.

components.name: ADIN1110
components.description: 10BASE-T1L single-pair Ethernet MAC-PHY on SPI (IEEE 802.3cg): 10 Mbit/s over one twisted pair up to 1.7 km. For long tethers and remote sensors on field robots, from MCUs without an Ethernet MAC.

components.name: CH340C
components.description: Very cheap crystal-free USB full-speed to UART bridge (up to 2 Mbaud, full modem lines). Good for a PC debug console, ROS serial link or bootloader port on a robot MCU board.

components.name: CH9102F
components.description: Crystal-free USB full-speed to UART bridge, up to 4 Mbaud, RTS/CTS flow control and a separate 1.8-5 V VIO. Good host USB link to 1.8/3.3/5 V robot MCUs; the TNOW pin can drive an RS-485 transceiver's DE.

components.name: CP2102N
components.description: Crystal-free USB full-speed to UART bridge, up to 3 Mbaud, with on-chip 5 V regulator and mature drivers on every OS. A robust host USB / debug-console link to a robot MCU.

components.name: FT232RL
components.description: Classic USB full-speed to UART bridge (up to 3 Mbaud) with internal EEPROM, clock and CBUS I/O, VCCIO 1.8-5.25 V. End of life: use the pin-compatible FT232RNL for new robot host-link designs.

components.name: VL53L0X
components.description: Classic single-zone ToF ranger: up to 2 m (1.2 m in default mode) with a 25° cone over I²C. Cheap and well supported by Arduino/Pololu/Adafruit libraries for robot obstacle detection; the VL53L1X/L4CX reach further.

specs.accuracy: 4% (1σ) at 1.2 m white, 33 ms; <±3% high-accuracy mode

components.name: VL53L1X
components.description: Long-distance single-zone ToF: up to 4 m in the dark at up to 50 Hz. A programmable ROI can narrow the 27° FoV or steer it. Popular for robot obstacle detection, drone altitude hold and people sensing over I²C.

components.name: VL53L4CD
components.description: Short-range, high-accuracy ToF: 1 mm to 1.3 m, 18° FoV, up to 100 Hz, with an autonomous low-power threshold mode. Good for cliff detection, wall following and close-in obstacle sensing on small robots.

components.name: VL53L4CX
components.description: Histogram-based single-zone ToF that reaches 6 m indoors on a white target, with an 18° FoV and output for up to 4 targets. Good for robot obstacle avoidance, cliff detection and drone landing behind cover glass.

components.name: VL6180X
components.description: Very short-range ToF proximity sensor (0-10 cm guaranteed) with an ambient light sensor, in a 4.8x2.8 mm part. Suits gripper object-present and edge detection. End of life: use the VL53L4CD for new designs.

components.name: VL53L5CX
components.description: 8x8-zone ToF depth sensor (45°x45° FoV, up to 4 m). A tiny low-res depth camera for robot obstacle avoidance, wall following, cliff and gesture detection over I²C; the host uploads ~84 KB firmware at boot.

components.name: VL53L7CX
components.description: Wide-angle 8x8-zone ToF sensor (60°x60°, 90° diagonal, up to 3.5 m). Pin and driver compatible with the VL53L5CX. Three cover 180° for SLAM, wall tracking and cliff detection on small robots.

components.name: VL53L8CX
components.description: Newer 8x8-zone ToF sensor (45°x45° FoV, up to 4 m) with better range in ambient light than the VL53L5CX and an I²C or SPI interface. Needs 3.3 V and 1.8 V rails, and its I/O is 1.2/1.8 V only.

components.name: TMF8801
components.description: Tiny single-zone direct ToF (2 cm to 2.5 m, ±5%) in a 3.6 x 2.2 mm OLGA module with on-chip histogram processing. Good for cheap cliff, bumper and short-range obstacle sensing on small robots over I²C.

components.name: TMF8820
components.description: 3x3-zone direct ToF (1 cm to 5 m) with a wide adjustable FoV (up to 63° diagonal) and up to two objects per zone, in a 4.6 x 2.0 mm OLGA module. Cheap wide-angle obstacle and presence sensing for robots over I²C.

components.name: TMF8821
components.description: Configurable 3x3, 4x4 or 3x6-zone direct ToF (1 cm to 5 m, up to 63° diagonal FoV) in a 4.6 x 2.0 mm OLGA module. Wide-angle obstacle mapping and gap finding for small robots over I²C.

components.name: TMF8828
components.description: 8x8-zone direct ToF (1 cm to 5 m, 41°x52° FoV) that can also run as a TMF8821 (3x3/4x4/3x6), in a 4.6 x 2.0 mm OLGA module. A depth-map style obstacle sensor for small robots over I²C.

components.name: AFBR-S50MV85G
components.description: 32-pixel indirect ToF module (850 nm) for 10 m+ ranging at up to 3 kHz frame rate, usable in 100-200 klx sunlight. Fast 1D/3D distance and motion sensing for outdoor robots; needs a Cortex-M host running Broadcom's driver over SPI.

components.name: TF-Luna
components.description: Low-cost, tiny single-point LiDAR: 0.2-8 m, 2° beam, 100 Hz over UART or I2C at 3.3 V logic. Good for robot obstacle and cliff sensing and drone altitude hold indoors.

components.name: TFmini-S
components.description: Small 12 m single-point LiDAR with a 10 cm blind zone, 2° beam and up to 1000 Hz. UART or I2C on a 4-pin cable. A step up from TF-Luna for longer range and outdoor use.

components.name: TFmini Plus
components.description: IP65-sealed 12 m single-point ranger with a 3.6° beam and up to 1000 Hz over UART (I2C also available). Rugged choice for outdoor robots, mowers and drone altitude hold.

components.name: TF02-Pro
components.description: Mid-range 40 m single-point LiDAR in an IP65 housing, 3° beam, 100 klux sunlight immunity and a 5-12 V supply. For outdoor robots, AGVs and drone altimeters that need range past 12 m.

components.name: LIDAR-Lite v4 LED
components.description: Garmin's 10 m optical ranger using a 940 nm LED (no laser), I2C at 3.3 V logic, >200 Hz. Has an on-board nRF52840 you can reprogram, plus ANT wireless. Good for indoor robots that need eye-safe ranging.

specs.accuracy: ±1 cm to 2 m, ±2 cm to 4 m, ±5 cm to 10 m (1σ repeatability)

components.name: TOFSense-F2
components.description: Low-cost 25 m single-point dToF ranger with a 1-2° beam, 100 Hz and 100 klux sunlight immunity. UART, I2C or I/O on one 4-pin GH1.25 plug. Cheap long-range option for robots and drones.

specs.eyeSafety: Laser 905 nm; Class 1 per Waveshare (Nooploop certification under review)

components.name: RPLIDAR A1
components.description: Classic low-cost 360° triangulation LiDAR, 12 m range at 5.5 Hz. Huge ROS community and examples make it the default first SLAM sensor for hobby and education robots; bulky and slow next to newer DTOF units.

components.name: RPLIDAR C1
components.description: Compact, cheap 360° DTOF LiDAR: 12 m range, 5 kHz at 10 Hz, ±30 mm, 40 klux sunlight tolerance, IP54, single 5 V supply. A strong modern replacement for the A1 on small ROS robots.

components.name: RPLIDAR A2
components.description: Thin (41 mm) 360° triangulation LiDAR with 16 kHz sampling and 0.225° resolution at 10 Hz, 12 m range. Denser scans than the A1 for indoor SLAM; brushless OPTMAG drive for long life.

components.name: RPLIDAR S2
components.description: Long-range 360° DTOF LiDAR: 30 m (10 m on black), 32 kHz at 10 Hz, ±30 mm, works in 80 klux sunlight, IP65. For outdoor and larger mobile robots that need dense scans at range.

components.name: LDROBOT LD19
components.description: Walnut-sized 360° DTOF LiDAR (D300 kit): 12 m, 4.5 kHz at 10 Hz, 30 klux, 5 V/180 mA. Streams scans over a TX-only UART with no commands needed, so it is easy to read from an MCU. Being replaced by the STL-19P.

specs.accuracy: ±45 mm mean (0.3–12 m), 10 mm std dev

components.name: YDLIDAR X2
components.description: Low-cost 360° triangulation scanner (8 m, 3 kHz) for indoor ROS robots, SLAM teaching and robot vacuums. Transmit-only 3.3 V UART at 115200 baud, motor speed set by a PWM/voltage pin.

components.name: YDLIDAR X4 Pro
components.description: 360° triangulation scanner with a 10 m range and 5 kHz sampling for indoor SLAM and navigation on ROS learning robots. Transmit-only 3.3 V UART at 128000 baud, with a PWM motor-speed pin.

components.name: YDLIDAR T-mini Plus
components.description: Tiny 38.6 mm ToF 360° scanner (12 m, 4 kHz, ±2 cm) with 60 klux ambient tolerance, for small robots, vacuums and ROS2 SLAM. Two-way 3.3 V UART at 230400 baud. Motor speed is set by command.

components.name: Unitree 4D LiDAR L1
components.description: Low-cost 360°×90° hemispherical 3D LiDAR (21,600 pts/s, up to 30 m) with a built-in IMU, for SLAM, mapping and obstacle avoidance on legged and wheeled robots. Point-LIO SLAM is supported.

components.name: Unitree 4D LiDAR L2
components.description: Hemispherical 360°×96° 3D LiDAR (64,000 pts/s, 30 m, ≤2 cm) with Ethernet UDP and a built-in IMU, for SLAM, mapping and obstacle avoidance on legged and wheeled robots. It is the L1's successor.

components.name: Livox Mid-360
components.description: Compact IP67 360°×59° 3D LiDAR (200k pts/s, 40 m @10% / 70 m @80%, 0.1 m blind zone) with a built-in IMU, for SLAM and obstacle avoidance on low-speed mobile robots, AGVs and quadrupeds.
